chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Abdullah ibn al-Mughira, from Sama'a, from Abu Basir — from them (peace be upon them) who said:

When you insert your hand into the vessel before washing it, there is no problem — except if the filth of urine or sexual impurity (janabah) has touched it. So if you insert your hand into the vessel while there is something of that on it, then pour out that water.

key_terms.أَهْرِقْ: pour out/spill — an imperative ruling to discard the water
key_terms.إِنَاء: vessel/container — the water vessel used for wudu or drinking
key_terms.جَنَابَة: janabah — the state of major ritual impurity requiring ghusl
key_terms.قَذَر: filth/impurity — here referring to ritual najasah
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ: there is no problem — a standard juridical formula meaning it is permissible

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to put an unwashed hand into a water vessel in Islam?
ai.summary: This hadith from the Imams (AS) addresses a common question in Islamic jurisprudence about ritual purity: whether dipping an unwashed hand into a water vessel renders the water impure. The ruling establishes that the default is permissibility — there is no harm — unless the hand carries specific major impurities (urine or janabah). In that case, the water becomes impure and must be discarded. This reflects the broader Shia jurisprudential principle that purity of water is preserved unless contaminated by a recognized najasah.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Abdullah Bin Al Mugheira, from Sama’at, from Abu Baseer, 
(It has been narrated) from them<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘When you enter your hand into the vessel before you wash it, so there is problem except if the filth happens to have hit it, either urine, or sexual impurity. So if you were to enter your hand into the vessel, and therein is something from that, then spill out that water’.
en.sarwar: 1. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ’Abd Allah ibn al-Mughirah from Sama‘ah from abu Basir the following: ‘‘(’A’immah), ‘Alayhim al-Salam, have said that it is permissible to place one’s hand in a water container before washing them, provided, urine or things from semen discharge has not reached them; otherwise, one must throw away such water.”
